llm.summary: The skill's behavior (sending PR diffs to configured model agents and auto-merging via a GH token) matches its stated purpose, but there are several metadata/instruction inconsistencies and privacy/credential risks you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (dual-model PR review, triage, optional auto-merge) aligns with what the script does: it fetches PRs, sends diffs to models via openclaw, and can merge using GH_TOKEN. However the registry metadata and SKILL.md disagree about required binaries (registry lists none; SKILL.md requires gh, python3, curl, openclaw). Also SKILL.md lists optional config envs (GUARDIAN_*) that are not declared in registry metadata. These inconsistencies are sloppy and worth double-checking but do not by themselves indicate malicious intent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and the script transmit PR diffs and file lists to configured OpenClaw agents (model providers), which is expected for a review skill but is sensitive: repository code (including potential secrets) is sent to whatever model endpoints OpenClaw is configured to use. The script also tries to fetch GH_TOKEN from gh auth if GH_TOKEN is not set, which reads local CLI auth state (could surface a token with broader scopes). The SKILL.md claims the token is never passed to models and diffs are truncated to 500 lines — both true in the script — but you must verify your OpenClaw agent/provider configuration before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only plus a shell script). Nothing is downloaded or extracted by the skill itself, which reduces install-time risk. However the script expects an 'openclaw' CLI and will call out to it — ensure that binary is official and configured to trusted providers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only required env var is GH_TOKEN, which is proportionate for a GitHub automation tool. The SKILL.md documents additional optional GUARDIAN_* variables for configuration. Two issues: (1) registry metadata did not mark the required binaries or primary credential consistently, and (2) the script will attempt to call 'gh auth token' to obtain a token if GH_TOKEN is unset — this may read a different token with broader scopes (local `gh` config), so prefer providing a fine-grained repo-scoped token explicitly.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request persistent system-wide privileges. It does not modify other skills or system configuration. It runs as a cron job (user-managed) or manually. Autonomous model invocation is normal for skills and is not by itself flagged.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: (1) Verify where your OpenClaw agents (agent names like 'keats' or 'openforge-cloud') actually route — only use providers you trust because PR diffs and file contents will be sent to them. (2) Create and supply a fine-grained GH_TOKEN scoped minimally (prefer repo-specific, and avoid using a token with org-wide or admin scopes). (3) Be aware the script will try to read 'gh auth token' if GH_TOKEN is not set — avoid allowing the script to fall back if that would expose a higher-privilege token. (4) Confirm the required binaries (openclaw, python3, curl, gh) are the official tools you expect; registry metadata omission is an inconsistency to resolve. (5) Consider running in --dry-run first and disabling auto-merge (GUARDIAN_AUTO_MERGE=false) until you audit logs and behavior. If you need more confidence, request the skill author to (a) publish a homepage/source repo, (b) clarify required binaries and primary credential in registry metadata, and (c) provide a list of OpenClaw agent endpoints the skill expects to use.
